name: Backup And Recovery Checklist
description: This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any backup and recovery task, implementation, or piece of work complete.
content:
This module is a short pre-completion checklist of specific items to verify before marking any backup and recovery task, implementation, or piece of work complete.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Surface known limitations of a chosen backup and recovery approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
2. Measure before optimizing any backup and recovery bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
3. Prefer explicit, readable backup and recovery solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. When backup and recovery guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
5. Keep backup and recovery changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to backup and recovery (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. Validate backup and recovery outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
8. Check that backup and recovery terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
9. Prefer the simplest backup and recovery approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. When multiple backup and recovery strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
11. State assumptions about backup and recovery explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
12. Document any non-obvious backup and recovery decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic backup and recovery advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new backup and recovery abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Avoid mixing unrelated backup and recovery concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not silently drop backup and recovery edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of backup and recovery correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these backup and recovery guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
